page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc6.10xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 3.1 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this server features 40 dedicated physical cores with a 1:1 thread-to-core ratio, providing 40 vCPUs. The hardware configuration includes 96.0 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 2.4 GB of memory per core. It operates on a KVM hypervisor, lacks local storage, and does not include any GPU accelerators. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place this instance in the average tier for its hardware class. It achieves a stress-ng single-core score of 1439.29 and a multi-core score of 38381.56. Memory bandwidth tests show 2132.58 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 105.52 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. In application-specific workloads, the instance handles 34.66 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and delivers a static web serving throughput of 23.2 GB/sec. For lightweight machine learning tasks, it processes 1928.13 tokens per second for prompt processing on a small 135M LLM, dropping to 57.07 tokens per second on a medium 7B model.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.hfc6.10xlarge offers high compute density with dedicated CPU resources, making it suitable for CPU-bound tasks that do not require massive memory footprints. However, the lack of local storage and GPU acceleration represents a clear tradeoff, requiring external block storage and limiting its utility for heavy deep learning training or large-scale LLM inference. This instance is best suited for workloads such as software compilation, multi-threaded decompression, database operations, and high-throughput static web serving.
